successCriteria.description: The leave repository implements all 8 methods (findById, findByEmployeeId, findByStatus, create, updateStatus, getBalance, upsertBalance, decrementBalance) against the pg pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts, each returning the typed model object (LeaveRequest | LeaveBalance) or null/empty array per its contract.

create inserts a new leave request with status 'DRAFT' and returns the persisted row mapped to the LeaveRequest model; updateStatus sets the correct reviewer/timestamp fields per status (APPROVED→approved_by/approved_at, REJECTED→rejected_by/rejected_at/rejection_reason, CANCELLED→cancelled_by/cancelled_at) and returns the updated row or null when no row matched.

upsertBalance performs an INSERT ON CONFLICT against the (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) unique constraint and returns the resulting LeaveBalance row; decrementBalance reduces used_days by the given amount for the matching (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) row and returns the updated row or null when no row matched.

Every returned row is mapped from snake_case DB columns to the camelCase model fields defined in src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts (e.g. employee_id→employeeId, leave_type_id→leaveTypeId, used_days→usedDays), with temporal columns converted to Date instances.
src/modules/leave/index.ts re-exports ILeaveRepository and LeaveRepository alongside the existing type exports, so both are reachable through the module barrel.

tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.repository.test.ts mocks pool.query and exercises all 8 repository methods, asserting correct SQL parameterization, row-to-model mapping, and null/empty-array returns when no rows match.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern using the pg pool imported from src/shared/db/connection.ts; no inline SQL or direct pool usage outside the repository (GP-001, HARNESS no-direct-db-outside-repository).
All SQL must use parameterized queries (pool.query with a values array) — no string interpolation or concatenation of user-supplied values into SQL text.
TypeScript strict mode applies: no implicit any, strict null checks; repository code must be fully typed with no `any` (HARNESS no-any rule — use unknown with type guards instead).

The authoritative model types are those in src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts; the repository must import and return those exact types (LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequestStatus, CreateLeaveRequestDto, UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto) — not redefine them.
Modules import only through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the repository and its interface must be exported via src/modules/leave/index.ts (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).

No unhandled promise rejections: all async repository methods must propagate errors as rejected promises that callers can catch (GP-006); the repository must not swallow or silently drop database errors.
outOfScope: Business logic and state-machine guards (DRAFT→SUBMITTED, SUBMITTED→APPROVED/REJECTED, balance decrement on approval) — these belong to the leave service in Phase 6, not the repository.
Audit record writing (GP-002) — the repository performs persistence only; audit logging is a cross-cutting concern handled by the service/orchestration layer in later phases.
Input validation (GP-003) and RBAC enforcement (GP-005) — these are API-boundary concerns handled by the controller/middleware in Phases 5 and 7, not the repository.
HTTP routes, controllers, and Fastify registration — Phase 7/8; the repository exposes only programmatic methods.
LeavePolicy repository and seed data — Phase 9; this phase covers only leave requests and leave balances data access.

ambiguities.description: The LeaveRequest.reason field is typed `string | undefined` in the model, while the DB column is nullable `text` (returns null for absent values). The row mapper must decide whether a DB null maps to undefined (matching the model) or whether the model's undefined should be persisted as null. This affects round-trip fidelity of the reason field.
options: Map DB null → undefined for reason to match the model's `string | undefined` type
Map DB null → null and tolerate the model allowing null (would require model change, out of scope)

entityInvariants.invariant: A newly created LeaveRequest always starts in the 'DRAFT' status with all reviewer/timestamp fields (approvedBy, approvedAt, rejectedBy, rejectedAt, rejectionReason, cancelledBy, cancelledAt) null — the repository's create method must never insert a request in any other initial status.

updateStatus sets reviewer fields exclusively per the target status: APPROVED populates only approved_by/approved_at (from dto.reviewerId and now), REJECTED populates only rejected_by/rejected_at/rejection_reason, CANCELLED populates only cancelled_by/cancelled_at; SUBMITTED and DRAFT set status only with no reviewer fields. The repository must not cross-populate reviewer fields for unrelated statuses.

A LeaveBalance row is unique per (employeeId, leaveTypeId, year); upsertBalance must never create duplicate rows for that triple — it either inserts or updates the existing row via the unique constraint conflict target.

decrementBalance only reduces used_days for an existing matching (employeeId, leaveTypeId, year) row; it must not insert a new row and must return null when no row matches, leaving the database unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.operation: findById(id) — read a single LeaveRequest by primary key
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the LeaveRequest mapped from the row, or null when no row matches; database errors propagate as rejected promises.

interfaceConstraints.operation: findByEmployeeId(employeeId) — list all LeaveRequests for an employee ordered by created_at DESC
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array (empty when no rows match, never null); database errors propagate as rejected promises.

interfaceConstraints.operation: findByStatus(status) — list LeaveRequests filtered by status
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array (empty when no rows match, never null); database errors propagate as rejected promises.

interfaceConstraints.operation: create(dto) — insert a new LeaveRequest with status DRAFT and return the persisted row
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the created LeaveRequest; database constraint violations (e.g. FK to leave_policies) propagate as rejected promises.

interfaceConstraints.operation: updateStatus(id, dto) — update a LeaveRequest's status and reviewer fields per the status-specific rules
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the updated LeaveRequest or null when no row matched the id; database errors propagate as rejected promises.

interfaceConstraints.operation: getBalance(employeeId, leaveTypeId, year) — read a single LeaveBalance by the natural key
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the LeaveBalance or null when no row matches; database errors propagate as rejected promises.

interfaceConstraints.operation: upsertBalance(balance) — insert or update a LeaveBalance on conflict of (employee_id, leave_type_id, year)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the resulting LeaveBalance row in both insert and update paths; repeated calls with the same natural key converge to one row (idempotent on the conflict target).

interfaceConstraints.operation: decrementBalance(employeeId, leaveTypeId, year, days) — reduce used_days on the matching LeaveBalance row
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the updated LeaveBalance or null when no row matched; database errors propagate as rejected promises.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The repository's return types and DTO parameter types must match the interfaces defined in src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts exactly — LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequestStatus, CreateLeaveRequestDto, UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto — including nullable/optional field handling (reason: string | undefined; reviewer/timestamp fields: ... | null).

The repository must obtain its database connection by importing the `pool` (pg.Pool) from src/shared/db/connection.ts and executing SQL via pool.query(text, params) — it must not instantiate its own Pool or read DATABASE_URL directly.

SQL against leave_requests must target the snake_case columns defined in migration 002 (employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, rejected_by, rejected_at, rejection_reason, cancelled_by, cancelled_at, created_at, updated_at) with status values restricted to the CHECK constraint set (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED).

SQL against leave_balances must target the snake_case columns defined in migration 003 (employee_id, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, used_days, accrued_days, year) and use the unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) as the ON CONFLICT target for upsertBalance.
The barrel export in src/modules/leave/index.ts must be extended (not replaced) to add ILeaveRepository and LeaveRepository while preserving the existing type re-exports from leave.model.ts.

The repository test must follow the existing test conventions established in tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.model.test.ts: ts-jest preset, describe/it/expect, relative import path ../../../../src/modules/leave/..., and testMatch under tests/**/*.test.ts.

integrationPoints.why: The repository depends on the shared database connection pool as its sole data-access entry point; it imports `pool` and runs all SQL through it.

The repository imports and returns the authoritative model types (LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequestStatus, CreateLeaveRequestDto, UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto) defined in Phase 2; it must not redefine them.

The repository interface and class must be exported through the module's public entry point so downstream phases (Phase 6 service, Phase 8 routes) can import them without reaching into module internals.
The ILeaveRepository interface established here is the contract the Phase 6 LeaveService will depend on and mock in its unit tests; the method signatures and return semantics must remain stable.
